<reason>Both sides were sharp and stayed on the motion, with clean Q/A formatting and equal clipping costs. B's central analytic move — a unit price is a level, not a change, so the "disclosure" is only unassembled arithmetic — framed the whole debate and survived. A's best counter (shoppers compare sideways across today's shelf, not backwards in time) was genuinely strong and forced B to work, but B's "was £2.00, now £1.50" reply landed hard: the industry itself uses delta framing whenever the delta flatters it, which reframes A's "consumer inattention" as manufactured inattention and, crucially, matches the motion's own time-limited window (A's rejoinder that promo deltas are dated and retailer-owned therefore partly boomerangs). B also defused the two mechanical objections cleanly: the baseline is an event (last weight sold under the product line) rather than a contested date, and retailers already hold weight/barcode records. A's strongest live route was substitution — flag the auditable route and cost recovery migrates to invisible ingredient downgrades — and A cleverly turned B's Carrefour evidence into a stigma-avoidance mechanism. But that route carries two costs: it rests on an unquantified magnitude claim, and A conceded the mandate would make shrinks rarer while also insisting the sticker doesn't change what shoppers buy, a tension B pressed directly ("firms don't spend political capital suppressing a sticker nobody reads"). A's "the rooms are connected" answer to B's lights-off analogy was the best available response but did not neutralize B's point that the absence of any rule, not this rule, is why quality cuts go unpoliced. B made the decisive clash easier to resolve.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's was/now framing reply: retailers already prove that change flags get read, and abandon delta framing precisely when the delta indicts them. It converted A's "shoppers ignore the label" defence into evidence of manufactured salience, and A's counter (promotions are dated and retailer-owned) inadvertently described the windowed flag the motion actually asks for.</best_rebuttal>
